scope_note: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's The Dalles campus in Wasco County. The fragment preserves the baseline 2023-2025 Google LLC and Design LLC tax-bill and assessed-value series and the documented $28.5 million water-infrastructure project, and adds only incremental evidence. Business Oregon supplies a dated three-facility operating snapshot and separately bounded Project 1 and Project 2 SIP forecasts; City of The Dalles planning files and contractor/permit records document later River Road construction without treating permit valuations as spending. A recipient record verifies one local grant. Searches of assessor and treasurer records, budgets and agreements, planning and permit systems, utility and environmental records, operator ESG/careers materials, contractors, suppliers, workforce sources, nonprofit recipients, archives and structured portals found no audited construction outlay, local supplier spend, facility payroll, employee residence, project-attributable utility cost or load, realized abatement ledger, same-scope public service cost, or fiscal net. Statewide Google totals and system-wide utility loads are excluded from campus claims.

sources.title: Oregon Business Development Commission December 2021 packet — Google/The Dalles SIP projects
sources.notes: The commission packet contains the December 10 staff memo and adopted SIP-21-01/SIP-21-02 resolutions. It reports a dated snapshot of three existing enterprise-zone facilities, approximately 120 Google employees, nearly 400 full-time onsite contractor/vendor jobs, and about $5 billion of cumulative investment. Each later SIP project is separately bounded, forecast at about $600 million and ten Google jobs, and capped at one contiguous complex with no more than a 500,000-square-foot footprint and 1,000,000 square feet of building area. The forecasts are not realized spending, employment, tax savings or public cost.

sources.title: Google data centers — The Dalles, Oregon
sources.notes: The operator page says Google opened its first owned-and-operated data center in The Dalles in 2006 and began building a fourth data center in 2015. Current investment, grant and volunteer totals are reported for Oregon rather than the selected campus or Wasco County and therefore are not normalized as project records.

sources.title: City of The Dalles notice of decision — SPR 512-22
sources.notes: The decision approves a Whiting-Turner/Design LLC data-center application at 3500 River Road for a 288,530-square-foot data-center building with office and supporting infrastructure. The approved area is a planning characteristic, not evidence of completion, operating area, project expenditure or occupied capacity.

sources.title: City of The Dalles site-plan application — SPR 538-23
sources.notes: The official planning record identifies Whiting-Turner, Design LLC, 3500 River Road, tax lot 2N13E28-700 and a proposed single-story approximately 290,000-square-foot data center. It establishes a later River Road development file but not final cost, payment, completion, employment, utility use or operation.

sources.title: GOR 1A & 2A Data Center
sources.notes: The concrete contractor identifies GOR 1A and 2A as a 290,000-gross-square-foot project completed in January 2024, with Whiting-Turner as client, Jacobs as architect and KPFF as structural engineer. The profile discloses no contract value, payments, payroll, worker residence, supplier geography or inventory allocation and is not converted to an economic record.

sources.title: Harder Mechanical Contractors — public permit summary for 3500 River Road
sources.notes: The contractor profile reproduces Oregon permit identifiers, issue dates, work descriptions, status and administrative valuations for Harder Mechanical work at 3500 River Road. Six issued phase-specific 2024-2025 permits are retained individually as reported permit values. They may overlap within the broader building program and are not invoices, audited spending, local procurement, economic output or an additive project total.

sources.title: OSHA inspection detail 1832411.015
sources.publisher: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.notes: The federal inspection record identifies Whiting-Turner at 3500 River Road, with an inspection opened June 18, 2025 and closed August 13, 2025 under commercial-building construction. It corroborates active construction at the address but reports no project worker count, hours, payroll, contract value, incident cost or local residence.

sources.title: Columbia Gorge Community College Board minutes — August 2024
sources.notes: The recipient's board minutes report receipt of a $50,000 Google grant dedicated to an updated simulation lab under construction at the college's The Dalles campus. This recipient-verified transfer is retained separately from statewide Google philanthropy totals and from negotiated tax-agreement payments.

sources.title: 2024 Economic Impact Study — Google Data Centers in Oregon
sources.notes: The report publishes Oregon data-center water consumption of 274.2 million gallons in 2022 and 302.4 million gallons in 2023, PUE of 1.09 and 84% carbon-free energy. The evidence contract has no direct actual-water-consumption or PUE metric, and the report does not allocate these figures to an inventory building; the values remain source metadata rather than being misclassified as projections or permitted capacity.

sources.title: Data Center Advisory Committee facilitator meeting summary — May 29, 2026
sources.notes: The official summary reports that Northern Wasco County PUD serves three data-center campuses and that its total system load rose from 90 MW in January 2016 to 277 MW in January 2026, driven substantially by data centers. Because neither load nor infrastructure cost is customer-allocated, no Google-campus electricity, tariff, utility investment or public-cost record is created.

sources.title: Google Careers — The Dalles data-center openings
sources.notes: The reviewed listing is for a Data Center Electrical Engineer in The Dalles and discloses a salary range. A current vacancy and offered range do not establish a filled campus position, annual payroll, employee residence, average realized wage or retention; no quantitative record is created.

sources.title: City of The Dalles adopted budget FY 2024-2025
sources.notes: The budget describes negotiated enterprise-zone payments, including historical initial and annual payments and allocations among local governments. The amounts are agreement-specific transfers with overlapping fiscal scopes, not property taxes paid, charitable grants, marginal public-service costs or a project-wide fiscal net, so they remain in the audit trail rather than being forced into an inexact metric.

project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — historical campus and later SIP projects separated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Google location and archive materials; Business Oregon commission packets, resolutions SIP-21-01 and SIP-21-02, and program tables; City planning records SPR 512-22 and SPR 538-23; and contractor project pages for 2005-2026. Queries used Google, Design LLC, Moraine Industries, GOR, River Road, 3500 River Road, tax lots 700 and 200, SIP-21-01, SIP-21-02, SPR 512-22 and SPR 538-23. Sources support the 2006 opening, 2015 fourth-building start, a December 2021 three-facility snapshot, two separately bounded SIP projects, and later roughly 289,000-square-foot River Road applications. They do not establish that the two SIP forecasts were fully realized or map every tax account, permit and inventory point to one building.
project_updates.project_description: Google's The Dalles data-center project is an operator-owned campus in The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon, rather than one selected building or the company's statewide portfolio. Google opened its first owned-and-operated data center there in 2006 and began building a fourth in 2015; Business Oregon later described three existing enterprise-zone facilities and two separately bounded SIP projects on tax lots 700 and 200. City approvals at 3500 River Road document roughly 289,000-square-foot data-center buildings, while each SIP resolution caps its approved complex at a 500,000-square-foot footprint and 1,000,000 square feet of building area.

project_updates.title: Fiscal audit — tax bills preserved; realized incentive cost and fiscal net unresolved
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Wasco County assessor/top-taxpayer reports for tax years 2022-2025; county BOCC minutes from 2021-2022; City tax-agreement pages and FY 2024-2025/FY 2025-2026 budgets; Business Oregon SIP applications, commission packets, statutory tables and resolutions; and Oregon tax-program materials. Searches used Google LLC party 155421, Design LLC party 130136, SIP-21-01, SIP-21-02, enterprise zone, community service fee, GAP, tax saved, tax paid and exempt value. The baseline six bills and six assessments remain unchanged. Agreements and budgets publish formulas and negotiated payments, but no reconciled realized abatement ledger, payment-status proof for the billed series, recipient-level distribution, same-scope marginal public-service cost or defensible net fiscal result was found; formulas and the approximately $1.9 billion 2021 exempt-value snapshot are not converted to tax savings.

project_updates.title: Construction and procurement audit — six permit valuations retained without summation
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: City of The Dalles HPRM planning files and agenda packets; Oregon ePermitting identifiers; BuildZoom's public permit summary; OSHA inspection 1832411.015; Whiting-Turner, Largo Concrete, Jacobs, KPFF and Harder Mechanical project or licensing pages; Port of The Dalles packets and lease references; and general contractor/supplier searches for 2021-2026. Exact searches covered 3500 River Road, GOR1A, GOR2A, 921-24-001277-PLM, 921-25-000109-PLM, 921-25-000303-MECH, 921-25-000304-MECH, 921-25-000313-MECH and 921-25-000314-MECH. Six issued administrative valuations are retained individually. No official downloadable project-wide permit ledger, contract value, invoice, audited construction outlay, worker hours, payroll, vendor payment, supplier geography or local-retention share was found; overlapping work descriptions prevent summation.

project_updates.title: Resource and environmental audit — campus allocation remains unavailable
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Northern Wasco County PUD board/news/tariff materials; Oregon Public Utility Commission jurisdiction information; Oregon Department of Energy Data Center Advisory Committee records; City water-infrastructure disclosures and budgets; Google's The Dalles water profile and 2024 Oregon impact study; Oregon DEQ environmental records and permit searches; and EPA facility searches for 2005-2026. Queries used Google, Design LLC, 3500 River Road, data center, substation, Taylor Lake, load, kWh, water, wastewater, ASR, emissions, generator and air permit. The baseline $28.5 million water-infrastructure record remains. Public sources disclose utility-system load and Oregon-level water consumption/PUE, but no customer tariff, campus annual electricity, project-attributable substation cost, selected-building water allocation, wastewater discharge, generator inventory or campus emissions. Direct actual water and PUE also lack matching evidence metrics, so those figures are not relabeled as projections or capacity.

project_updates.title: Workforce audit — dated headcount added; payroll and residence remain gaps
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Business Oregon employment/payroll material; Google careers and operator location pages; WorkSource/first-source hiring references in SIP records; Oregon workforce reports; and local education/workforce recipient records for 2005-2026. Queries used Google The Dalles, Design LLC, employees, contractors, vendors, salary, payroll, FTE, first source, apprenticeship and job titles. The December 2021 approximately 120 Google employees and nearly 400 onsite contractor/vendor jobs are retained as distinct campus stocks. Live vacancies and salary ranges are not filled positions or realized payroll. No current facility headcount, occupation table, annual payroll, hours, turnover, employee residence, local-hire realization or building allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Community audit — one recipient-verified local grant added
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Google community and location disclosures; Columbia Gorge Community College board materials; North Wasco County School District and Columbia Gorge ESD records; The Dalles-Wasco County Library and local nonprofit pages; city/county budget references; and recipient searches for grants, gifts, robotics, STEM, education, housing and volunteer support from 2006-2026. CGCC verifies receipt of a $50,000 Google grant for its The Dalles simulation lab. Other operator totals are statewide, cumulative, undated, co-funded or lack a recipient ledger and are not allocated to the campus. No complete annual Wasco County grant register, in-kind valuation or campus-attributable volunteer-hour series was found.

project_updates.title: Investment and supplier audit — cumulative actual separated from forecasts
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Business Oregon project/company material; Google operator investment pages; City and county economic-development records; contractor portfolios; planning and permit records; and supplier/carrier/procurement searches from 2005-2026. The 2021 state memo supports approximately $5 billion cumulative investment in the three existing facilities and two separate approximately $600 million SIP project forecasts. Statewide current investment totals are excluded, and permit valuations are not substituted for expenditure. The nearly 400 onsite contractor/vendor jobs establish an operations stock only; no vendor roster, contract amount, local purchase share, supplier output, carrier payment, local payroll or audited equipment-versus-construction split was found.

project_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — only descriptive county benchmarks qualify
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: repository BEA/BLS County Economic Core panel for 2001-2024, facility-study county exclusions, and the project-specific direct-evidence categories documented above. The selected campus opened in 2006, leaving a five-year 2001-2005 pre-period in the available panel. After direct-source searches did not produce causal county outcomes, three reproducible inverse-distance-weighted 20-county comparison gaps are retained only as low-confidence descriptive context with fit-sensitivity envelopes. No input-output supplier, resource, construction-employment, public-cost, induced-household or net-fiscal model is eligible because project-specific expenditure, payroll, consumption and same-scope cost anchors are missing. No records requests were made.
